meaning: marks completed action or new change
core: 了 (le) marks that an action has finished, or that a new situation has just come into being. Learners often overuse it for every past action, or forget it when reporting a fresh change.

sentences.why: A diner tells the waiter they have finished choosing dishes. The 了 signals the ordering process is complete and the waiter can take the order.
sentences.tip: Said with a slight nod to the waiter.

sentences.pinyin: wǒ dào dì tiě zhàn le
sentences.en: I've arrived at the subway station.
sentences.why: You update a friend who is waiting for you. The 了 marks the new state of having just arrived.
sentences.tip: Common in WeChat; add 马上来 if you want to say 'coming right up'.

sentences.pinyin: wǒ jīn tiān chī le huǒ guō
sentences.why: You tell a roommate about your day. The 了 after the verb marks the action as completed.
sentences.tip: Do not add 了 again at the end; one 了 after the verb is enough here.

sentences.pinyin: bào gào wǒ yǐ jīng xiě wán le
sentences.en: I've already finished writing the report.
sentences.why: You update a colleague waiting for your report. The 了 marks completion and reassures them.

sentences.pinyin: hǎo de, wǒ zhī dào le
sentences.why: You acknowledge an instruction from your boss. The 了 signals you have received and understood the information.
sentences.tip: Add 马上办 if you want to show you will act immediately.

sentences.pinyin: xià yǔ le, wǒ men huí jiā ba
sentences.en: It's raining now, let's go home.
sentences.why: You notice rain has just started and want your child to go inside. The 了 marks the new weather situation.
sentences.tip: Rising intention on 下雨了 to draw attention.

sentences.pinyin: zhè jiàn yī fú wǒ mǎi le
sentences.en: I'll take this piece of clothing.
sentences.why: You have decided to buy an item. The  here signals a firm decision and commitment.
sentences.tip: Said firmly; shop assistants hear this often.

sentences.zh: 我在开会，一会儿打给你。
sentences.pinyin: wǒ zài kāi huì, yī huì er dǎ gěi nǐ
sentences.en: I'm in a meeting, I'll call you back later.
sentences.why: You explain why you cannot talk now. 了 is not needed here because you are describing an ongoing action, not a completed one.
sentences.tip: This is a common trap: do not add 了 just because you are busy.

sentences.situation: On the street · to a stranger
sentences.zh: 前面的路坏了，要绕路走。
sentences.pinyin: qián miàn de lù huài le, yào rào lù zǒu
sentences.en: The road ahead is broken, you need to take a detour.
sentences.why: You warn a stranger about a road problem. The 了 marks the new bad state of the road.
sentences.tip: Use 坏了 to say something is broken or out of order.

sentences.zh: 合同我们已经看过了，没有问题。
sentences.pinyin: hé tóng wǒ men yǐ jīng kàn guò le, méi yǒu wèn tí
sentences.en: We have already reviewed the contract, no problems.
sentences.why: You confirm to a client that the contract has been checked. The 了 signals completion and gives the client confidence.
sentences.tip: Add 请放心 for extra reassurance.

quiz.prompt: You just got to a coffee shop where your friend is waiting. Tell them you've arrived.
quiz.explain: 了 marks the new state of having just arrived.

quiz.prompt: A waiter asks if you're ready to order. Tell them you are ready.
quiz.explain: 了 signals the ordering process is complete.

quiz.prompt: Your boss tells you to send a report today. Acknowledge politely that you understand.
quiz.explain: 了 shows you have received and understood the instruction.

quiz.prompt: You are on the street and notice it just started raining. Tell your friend it's raining and suggest going home.
accept: 开始下雨了，我们回去吧。
quiz.explain: 了 marks the new weather situation that just changed.

quiz.prompt: 你的朋友问你：“昨天你做什么了？” 用一句话回答，说你昨天吃了火锅。
accept: 昨天我和朋友吃了火锅。
quiz.explain: 了 after the verb marks a completed past action.

quiz.prompt: 你的同事问你：“报告写完了吗？” 回答说你已经写完了，没有问题。
quiz.explain: 了 signals the report is finished and reassures the colleague.
